subject: Art & Design
title: Caravaggio: Light, Shadow, and Scandal
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Caravaggio: Light, Shadow, and Scandal.

hook.text: Caravaggio killed a man in a street brawl, fled Rome, and kept painting masterpieces on the run.

buildup.text: He pioneered chiaroscuro — extreme contrast between deep shadow and dramatic spotlight.

discovery.text: He used real street people as models for saints and biblical figures. The church was horrified.

twist.text: One painting was rejected because the Virgin Mary's model was a drowned prostitute from the Tiber.

climax.text: Despite the scandals, his dramatic lighting influenced Rembrandt, Velázquez, and all of Baroque art.

punchline.text: Art's greatest lighting technician was also its worst citizen.

quiz.question: What technique did Caravaggio pioneer?
options: Chiaroscuro — extreme contrast of light and shadow

details.summary: Caravaggio (1571-1610) revolutionized painting with dramatic chiaroscuro — extreme contrasts of light and dark that made scenes leap from black backgrounds. He used ordinary people as models for saints and biblical figures, bringing gritty realism to religious art.
details.whyItMatters: Caravaggio invented modern dramatic lighting in painting. His influence spread across Europe through followers called Caravaggisti, and his chiaroscuro technique remains fundamental to photography, cinema, and visual storytelling today.
takeaways: Pioneered chiaroscuro with extreme light-dark contrasts
Used ordinary people as models for sacred figures
His dramatic lighting influenced photography and cinema

faq.question: What is chiaroscuro?
faq.answer: The use of strong contrasts between light and dark to model three-dimensional forms and create dramatic mood. Caravaggio pushed this to extremes — figures emerge from pitch-black backgrounds, spotlit as if by a single harsh light source, creating theatrical intensity.

faq.question: Why was Caravaggio controversial in his own time?
faq.answer: Church patrons rejected paintings showing saints with dirty feet and wrinkled faces. His models were recognizable street people. His violent temper led to brawls, a murder, and flight from Rome. Despite his genius, his personal life was a series of scandals and criminal charges.
